Web · /login · /forgot-password · /reset-password · /change-password

Unauthenticated screens — one shared shell

The login scene is a fully designed system in globals.css. Sign-in used all of it; the other three unauthenticated screens used only the background and rebuilt a plainer card. Anyone who clicked "Forgot password?" watched the branding change mid-flow.

Side by side

Captured from the real routes on a local dev server at 1280×900, device scale 2, after entrance animations settled. The baseline came from git stash of only these four files, so the rest of the working tree was identical between runs.

Forgot password

Reset password

Sign in — the reference

Already correct. Included to show the target the other three now match.

What changed, and why

Presentational only. No auth logic, form submission, validation, token handling, passkey flow, or redirect behavior was touched.

Three screens ignored the design system that already existed

Was

globals.css defines a complete login scene: .login-card is a translucent material with a blurred backdrop and a bright top edge, .login-materialize settles it in, .login-rise staggers content, and .login-lockup-title puts the wordmark on the scene. Sign-in used all of it. Forgot password, reset password, and forced password change used only .login-bg and built a plain shadow-2xl card instead.

Now

src/components/auth/AuthScreen.tsx owns the scene, the noise layer, the lockup, and the card. All four screens render through it and supply a subtitle plus their form.

Three of four had no heading element

Was

Forgot, reset, and forced change titled the page with CardTitle, which renders a div. Measured in the browser: main h1 returned nothing on all three.

Now

The shell renders a real h1. This is the same defect found in item detail and booking detail earlier today — four of the app's surfaces had no page heading.

A 380-character data URI was pasted into four files

Was

The film-grain texture over the gradient is an inline SVG feTurbulence data URI. It appeared verbatim in all four screens; changing the grain meant editing four files and hoping none drifted.

Now

One named constant in the shell. A grep for feTurbulence across src/ now returns exactly one file.

The footer is a slot, not a special case

Was

Sign-in carries an "Access is by invitation only" line below the card, on the scene rather than inside it. No other screen has one.

Now

AuthScreen takes an optional footer, so sign-in keeps it without the shell hardcoding a sign-in-specific element.

Verification

  • TypeScript: npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false clean.
  • Lint: npx eslint clean on all five files.
  • Full suite: npx vitest run tests/ — 3628 passing, 0 failing, 535 files.
  • New contract test: tests/auth-screen-source.test.ts, 5 assertions covering the shared shell, the single noise copy, the login material, the h1, and the CSS the shell depends on.
  • Captures are from the real routes, not a harness — these screens are unauthenticated, so the dev server renders them directly. Measured per screen: logo size, whether the logo is inside the card, h1 presence and computed size, and the card's computed backdrop-filter.
  • Baseline method: git stash push scoped to only these four paths, so unrelated working-tree changes were byte-identical across both capture runs. Restore verified before continuing.

What this does not prove

  • Forced password change was not captured. /change-password requires an authenticated session, which is the standing local limitation. It was converted with the same shell and passes the source contract, but has no visual pair here.
  • Unexercised: no form was submitted. The passkey flow, email discovery, token validation, and error and success states were not driven — only the resting render of each screen.
  • A first capture attempt returned nulls for forgot-password and was discarded as a dev-server compile artifact rather than reported as a finding. The numbers here are from a re-capture after the route had compiled.
  • Not converted: src/app/login/loading.tsx deliberately keeps a minimal variant — logo, wordmark, spinner, no card. Routing it through the shell would render an empty card. It already shares the lockup treatment.
  • Still outside any shell: /support and /privacy are standalone public pages using neither the auth scene nor the app shell. They were out of scope here.
